content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides that Matthew 1:20 is underdetermined after both sides answered, so it treats the verse as answered rather than as an unanswered witness.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"‘A verse the judge says was answered is not counted’ — I weighed whether the text was counting Matthew 1:20 as an unanswered witness, which would require quoting the pressing sentence, or merely saying it was answered; the words say answered, so no quote is required.","why":"The judge text says the challenger and defender answered, so under K-G4 the verse is not counted as an unanswered witness and no quoted pressing sentence is required."}
